proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\), and deterministic pilot dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\), and condition on the two pilot releases.  By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\), the true nuisances belong to the nonempty closed convex sets \(\mathcal C_\pi\) and \(\mathcal C_\mu\), using Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}propensity\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\).  Hence the metric projections \(\bar\pi\) and \(\bar\mu\) lie in those sets.  In particular, their ranges and H\"older radii equal the restrictions required by Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\), uniformly in the realized Gaussian pilot noises.

Put \(\ell=h/k^{1/d}\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}spline\text{-}population\text{-}algebra}\) supplies \(\vartheta_\tau\in\mathbb R^{p_\gamma}\) such that
\[
 \rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0),
 \qquad \|\vartheta_\tau\|_2\le C,
\tag{1}
\]
and, writing \((Q^\circ,R^\circ)=\mathbb E_Q[(T_{*,Q},T_{*,R})\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu]\),
\[
 \|R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\|_2\le Cb_0,
 \qquad
 \|Q^\circ-Q^0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\ell^{2\alpha},
\tag{2}
\]
where
\[
 b_0=h^\gamma+\ell^{\alpha+\beta}+h^\gamma\ell^\alpha,
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\lambda_0:=\kappa(1-\kappa),
 \qquad
 \|R^\circ\|_2\le C.
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\) and \(0<\kappa<1/2\) give \(\lambda_0>0\).  Also \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\), since \(k\ge1\).

Let
\[
 x_\eta=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M_h=mh^d,
\]
and define
\[
 a_0=
 \sqrt{\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}\left(1+\frac{k}{M_h}\right)}
 +\frac{x_\eta}{M_h}
 +\frac{\sqrt{k}\,x_\eta^{3/2}}{M_h^{3/2}}
 +\frac{kx_\eta^2}{M_h^2},
\tag{4}
\]
\[
 g_0=\frac{\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)x_\eta}}{m\epsilon_n}
       \{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Choose \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\), where \(C_0\) is the constant in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}localized\text{-}score\text{-}concentration\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\).  The hypothesis \(M_h\ge C_S^2x_\eta\) then implies \(M_h\ge C_0x_\eta\), so that lemma yields, conditionally on the pilots, an event \(E_S\) with
\[
 \Pr_Q(E_S\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,
 \qquad
 \|T_*-T_*^\circ\|_2\le C a_0
 \quad\hbox{on }E_S.
\tag{6}
\]
This application is valid for every finite \(k\); no comparison between \(k\) and \(M_h\) is used.

The Gaussian vector in the main-block release has the fixed dimension
\(D_*=p_\gamma^2+p_\gamma\).  For a scalar standard normal \(Z\), completing
the square in its density gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
 \mathbb E e^{tZ}
 =(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-z^2/2+tz}\,dz
 =e^{t^2/2}.
\]
Markov's inequality with \(t=u\), applied also to \(-Z\), therefore gives
\(\Pr\{|Z|>u\}\le2e^{-u^2/2}\).  Since
\(\|Z_*\|_2\le\sqrt{D_*}\max_j|Z_{*,j}|\), a coordinate union bound with
\(u=\sqrt{2\log(4D_*/\eta)}\) yields
\[
 \Pr\{\|Z_*\|_2>\sqrt{2D_*\log(4D_*/\eta)}\}\le\eta/2.
\]
The dimension \(D_*\) depends only on \(d\) and \(\gamma\), and
\(0<\eta<1/4\), so \(\log(4D_*/\eta)\le C\log(8/\eta)=Cx_\eta\).
Consequently,
\[
 \Pr\{\|Z_*\|_2>C\sqrt{x_\eta}\}\le\eta/2.
\tag{7}
\]
The declared parameter ranges \(0<\delta_n<1/2\), \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\), and the definitions of \(c_{\delta_n}\) and \(\epsilon_n^\circ\) imply
\[
 c_{\delta_n}\le C\sqrt{\log(1/\delta_n)},
 \qquad
 (\epsilon_n^\circ)^{-1}\le2\epsilon_n^{-1}.
\tag{8}
\]
The unchanged sensitivity conclusion of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), together with (7)--(8) and the Gaussian scale in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\), therefore gives an event \(E_G\) such that
\[
 \Pr(E_G\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\ge1-\eta/2,
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde T_*-T_*\|_2\le Cg_0
 \quad\hbox{on }E_G.
\tag{9}
\]
Consequently, on \(E=E_S\cap E_G\), the union bound gives conditional probability at least \(1-\eta\), and the componentwise reconstruction of \((\widetilde Q,\widetilde R)\), (6), and (9) give
\[
 \|\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\|\widetilde R-R^\circ\|_2
 \le e_0:=C(a_0+g_0).
\tag{10}
\]

We first consider the stable case
\[
 C\ell^{2\alpha}+e_0\le\lambda_0/2,
\tag{11}
\]
where the constant is enlarged, if necessary, to be the one in (2).  For every unit vector \(v\), (2), (3), and (10) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widetilde Qv\|_2
 &\ge \|Q^0v\|_2
      -\|(Q^\circ-Q^0)v\|_2
      -\|(\widetilde Q-Q^\circ)v\|_2\\
 &\ge\lambda_0-C\ell^{2\alpha}-e_0
 \ge\lambda_0/2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Thus \(\sigma_{\min}(\widetilde Q)\ge\lambda_0/2>\lambda_0/4\).  The singular-value floor in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) is inactive, so \(\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}=\widetilde Q\) and
\[
 \|\widetilde Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2/\lambda_0.
\tag{13}
\]
Using (1), inserting and subtracting \(R^\circ\), \(Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\), and \(\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\), and then applying (2), (10), (13), and the fixed bound on \(\rho_h(x_0)\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|
 &\le \|\rho_h(x_0)\|_2\|\widetilde Q^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \|\widetilde R-\widetilde Q\vartheta_\tau\|_2\\
 &\le C\bigl(
       \|R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\|_2
       +\|\widetilde R-R^\circ\|_2
       +\|\widetilde Q-Q^\circ\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\vartheta_\tau\|_2
       \bigr)\\
 &\le C(b_0+a_0+g_0).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]

If (11) fails, then either \(C\ell^{2\alpha}>\lambda_0/4\) or \(e_0>\lambda_0/4\).  In the first alternative, positivity of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) yields
\[
 \ell^{\alpha+\beta}
 =\left(\ell^{2\alpha}\right)^{(\alpha+\beta)/(2\alpha)}
 \ge c_1>0;
\tag{15}
\]
in the second, \(a_0+g_0\ge c_2>0\).  Hence in either alternative
\[
 b_0+a_0+g_0\ge c_*>0.
\tag{16}
\]
The singular-value floor always gives
\(\|\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le4/\lambda_0\).  By (3) and (10), \(\|\widetilde R\|_2\le C+e_0\); moreover \(|\tau_Q(x_0)|\le1\) by the range in the definition of \(\tau_Q\).  Therefore, on \(E\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|
 &\le \|\rho_h(x_0)\|_2
       \|\widehat Q_{\mathrm{DP}}^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
       \|\widetilde R\|_2+|\tau_Q(x_0)|\\
 &\le C(1+a_0+g_0)
 \le C'(b_0+a_0+g_0),
 \end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
where (16) justifies the last inequality.

Choose \(C_B,C_S,C_G\) at least as large as the constants in (14) and (17), while retaining \(C_S\ge\sqrt{C_0}\).  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\) then give
\[
 B(h,k)=C_Bb_0,\qquad
 S(h,k,\eta)=C_Sa_0,\qquad
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)=C_Gg_0.
\tag{18}
\]
Equations (14), (17), and (18) prove the asserted raw-estimator error inequality on \(E\).  Its conditional failure probability is at most \(\eta\), uniformly over the realized pilots and every finite \(k\); integration over both pilot blocks proves the unconditional assertion, including all pilot and main-block Gaussian randomness.  Finally, clipping the released center in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) is downstream post-processing and does not enter this lemma: the controlled object throughout is the unchanged raw estimator \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)\).

Fix \(0<h\le r_0\), a finite integer \(k\ge1\) satisfying \(mh^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), and integers \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\), applied to Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\), proves that \(C_n(h,k)\) is replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private; clipping the released center and intersecting with \([-1,1]\) are post-processing.

For \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), set
\[
 R=R_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)
      +G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
\]
and define
\[
 E_Q=\left\{
 |\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\tau_Q(x_0)|\le R
 \right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
All three summands defining \(R\) are nonnegative by Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\).  The effective-sample condition permits application of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\), which gives
\[
 \Pr_Q(E_Q)\ge1-\eta.
\tag{2}
\]
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) gives \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\), and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\) therefore gives
\[
 \theta_Q:=\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0).
\tag{3}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) implies \(-1\le Y(1)-Y(0)\le1\) almost surely.  Monotonicity of conditional expectation preserves these bounds, so
\[
 \theta_Q\in[-1,1].
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(\Pi(t)=\max\{-1,\min\{1,t\}\}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) sets
\(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)=\Pi(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k))\).  For every \(\theta\in[-1,1]\),
\[
 |\Pi(t)-\theta|\le|t-\theta|.
\tag{5}
\]
Indeed, equality holds when \(t\in[-1,1]\); if \(t>1\), then \(0\le1-\theta\le t-\theta\); and if \(t<-1\), then \(0\le\theta+1\le\theta-t\).  Combining (1), (3), (4), and (5), on \(E_Q\) one has
\[
 |\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\theta_Q|
 \le|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)-\theta_Q|
 \le R.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\theta_Q\) belongs both to
\([\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}-R,\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}+R]\) and, by (4), to \([-1,1]\).  The interval definition and (6) imply
\[
 E_Q\subseteq\{\theta_Q\in C_n(h,k)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Moreover, on every transcript, including outside \(E_Q\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\in[-1,1]\) and \(R\ge0\).  Hence \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}\) lies in both closed intervals whose intersection defines \(C_n(h,k)\), proving that \(C_n(h,k)\) is always a nonempty closed interval.

Taking probabilities in (7), using (2), and then taking the infimum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) yields
\[
 \inf_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \Pr_Q\{\tau_Q^{\mathrm c}(x_0)\in C_n(h,k)\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
The probability in (2) integrates the sampling law of all three blocks and every pilot and moment Gaussian release, by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}uniform\text{-}remainder\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\).  No rank condition relating \(k\) to \(mh^d\) was introduced.

We first transfer the ordinary two-law construction in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\) to the attainable class.  In the notation of that proof, let
\[
 p_* =\min\{1/4,L_\mu/2\}>0,
 \qquad
 g_h(x)=a_*h^\gamma\varphi((x-x_0)/h),
\tag{1}
\]
where \(\varphi\) is the displayed nonnegative \(C^\infty\) bump supported on \([-1,1]^d\), \(\varphi(0)=1\), and \(a_*>0\) is chosen there so that, for every \(0<h\le r_0\),
\[
 g_h\in\mathcal H^\gamma(L_\tau;\mathcal X),
 \qquad 0\le g_h\le p_*/2,
 \qquad g_h(x_0)=a_*h^\gamma.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(Q_0,Q_h\) be the same two full-data laws.  Under both, \(X\) is uniform on \(\mathcal X\), \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\kappa)\), and \(A\) is conditionally independent of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) given \(X\).  Under \(Q_0\), the potential outcomes are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with common mean \(p_*\).  Under \(Q_h\), they are conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(0)\mid X=x]=p_*,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{Q_h}[Y(1)\mid X=x]=p_*+g_h(x).
\tag{3}
\]
In both laws define \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).

We check every member property in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}attainable\text{-}law\text{-}class}\).  The last construction gives Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\), and the stipulated conditional independence gives Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}ignorability}\).  Both potential outcomes take values in the common support \(\{0,1\}\), so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) holds; their Bernoulli probabilities are valid and strictly positive because (2) implies
\[
 0<p_*\le p_*+g_h(x)\le3p_*/2\le3/8<1.
\tag{4}
\]
Since \(0<\kappa<1/2\), the constant propensity \(\pi_Q\equiv\kappa\) satisfies Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\), and its H\"older norm is \(\kappa\le L_\pi\) by the proposition's premise, giving Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}propensity\text{-}holder}\).  The control regression is the constant \(p_*\), whose H\"older norm is at most \(L_\mu/2\), so Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\) holds.  The contrast is zero under \(Q_0\) and equals \(g_h\) under \(Q_h\), so (2) gives Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}cate\text{-}holder}\).  Finally, the design density equals one almost everywhere, which is precisely Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}uniform\text{-}design}\).  Therefore
\[
 Q_0,Q_h\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}.
\tag{5}
\]

Let \(P_0,P_h\) be the corresponding one-record observed laws.  The exact calculations in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}ordinary\text{-}lower}\), which use the support inclusion guaranteed by \(x_0\in[r_0,1-r_0]^d\) and \(h\le r_0\), give finite positive constants \(C_\chi,C_v\) such that
\[
 \chi^2(P_h\|P_0)=C_\chi h^{2\gamma+d},
 \qquad
 \|P_h-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=C_vh^{\gamma+d},
\tag{6}
\]
and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}pointwise\text{-}identification}\) gives
\[
 |\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)-\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0)|
 =a_*h^\gamma.
\tag{7}
\]
The product-divergence calculation and private Hamming-transport argument in that theorem, using \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\) and \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), provide constants \(c_1,c_2\in(0,r_0]\) such that
\[
 h_1=c_1n^{-1/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 h_2=c_2\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-1}\}^{1/(\gamma+d)}
\tag{8}
\]
satisfy, for every replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-private release kernel \(\mathsf K\),
\[
 \|P_{h_j}^n\mathsf K-P_0^n\mathsf K\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1/8,
 \qquad j\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{9}
\]

Take any \(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\) with release kernel \(\mathsf K\), and fix either \(h=h_1\) or \(h=h_2\).  Write
\[
 \theta_0=\tau_{Q_0}^{\mathrm c}(x_0),
 \quad \theta_h=\tau_{Q_h}^{\mathrm c}(x_0),
 \quad \nu_0=P_0^n\mathsf K,
 \quad \nu_h=P_h^n\mathsf K.
\]
Membership (5) and attainable-class honesty give
\[
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C\}\ge1-\eta,
 \qquad
 \nu_h\{\theta_h\in C\}\ge1-\eta.
\]
By (9), \(\nu_0\{\theta_h\in C\}\ge1-\eta-1/8\).  The union bound and \(0<\eta<1/4\) therefore yield
\[
 \nu_0\{\theta_0\in C,\theta_h\in C\}
 \ge1-2\eta-1/8>3/8.
\tag{10}
\]
On the event in (10), the interval \(C\) contains both target values, so (7) implies \(\operatorname{length}(C)\ge a_*h^\gamma\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_0}[\operatorname{length}(C)]
 \ge(3a_*/8)h^\gamma.
\tag{11}
\]
Apply (11) at both bandwidths in (8).  Because the same null law \(Q_0\) is used in both comparisons, taking their maximum, then the supremum over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), and finally the infimum over \(C\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), proves
\[
 \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})
 \ge c\left[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \vee\left\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\right\}\right].
\tag{12}
\]

For the upper bound, put
\[
 a_n=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad
 b_n=1\wedge\left[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}
          \vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right].
\tag{13}
\]
Choose the deterministic minimizing \((h,k)\) specified by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}phase\text{-}sensitive\text{-}expected\text{-}length}\) and any fixed deterministic pilot dimensions.  The clipped center in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) lies in \([-1,1]\), and its deterministic radius is nonnegative, so the intersection defining the resulting \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) contains its center on every transcript.  Thus it is literally a nonempty random interval.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}private\text{-}release\text{-}and\text{-}sensitivity}\) and Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}honest\text{-}private\text{-}pointwise\text{-}interval\text{-}unrestricted\text{-}rank}\) show that \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), while the phase-sensitive theorem gives, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}})]
 \le C_{\mathrm{HO}}a_n.
\tag{14}
\]
The direct interval \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) in Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}full\text{-}class\text{-}direct\text{-}regression\text{-}upper}\) is replacement private, nonempty, and honest on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}attainable\text{-}inclusion}\) restricts those properties to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), so \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\in\mathfrak C_n^{\mathrm{att}}\), and
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\}]
 \le C_{\mathrm{dir}}b_n.
\tag{15}
\]
Define a public deterministic selector that releases \(C_n^{\mathrm{HO}}\) when \(a_n\le b_n\), and releases \(C_n^{\mathrm{dir}}(h_n)\) otherwise.  The choice uses only public parameters and executes exactly one mechanism, so it creates no privacy composition.  Equations (14)--(15) give
\[
 \mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}})
 \le\max\{C_{\mathrm{HO}},C_{\mathrm{dir}}\}\min\{a_n,b_n\},
\tag{16}
\]
which is the asserted upper inequality after renaming the maximum constant.

It remains to verify the stated strict-improvement regime.  Suppose \(q\ge\gamma\), \(\beta<\gamma<2\beta\), and \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}=n^{c_{\mathrm p}}\), where \(c_{\mathrm p}\) obeys the two restrictions in the proposition.  Then \(s=q/2\ge\gamma/2\), and
\[
 \frac{\gamma}{2}>
 \frac{d/4}{1+d/(2\gamma)}.
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\), with \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}=\gamma\), therefore yields
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+d)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{17}
\]
The inequality \(c_{\mathrm p}< (\gamma+2d)/(2\gamma+d)\) makes \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) dominate \(r_{\mathrm{np}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and \(r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) always dominates \(r_{\mathrm{reg}}\).  Since \(c_{\mathrm p}>0\), saturation is eventually inactive, and hence
\[
 a_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}.
\tag{18}
\]
Likewise, \(c_{\mathrm p}< (\beta+d)/(2\beta+d)\) makes the privacy term dominate the sampling term in \(b_n\), so
\[
 b_n=n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\beta/(\beta+d)}.
\tag{19}
\]
Finally, \(\gamma<2\beta\) is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\beta}{\beta+d}>\frac{\gamma}{\gamma+2d}.
\]
Equations (18)--(19) thus give
\[
 \frac{b_n}{a_n}
 =n^{-c_{\mathrm p}\{\beta/(\beta+d)-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)\}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves the strict polynomial improvement.  Every comparison above is made on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\); it does not close or alter the separate full-class frontier.

prose_updates.tldr: The raw private higher-order estimator retains its uniform finite-sample remainder bound because clipping occurs only after estimation.  Clipping the released center to \([-1,1]\) cannot increase its error from the bounded causal CATE and makes the reported higher-order set a nonempty random interval on every transcript.  On the uniform-design attainable class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), this interval achieves \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\), while the fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval proved on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) remains valid after restriction.  A public selector gives the attainable upper \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\); the uniform-design witness from the ordinary lower bound belongs to the attainable class and gives the stated two-sided nonsharp bracket.  On the unchanged full class, only the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower and \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper are certified, and the sharp private frontier remains the sole open statement.

project_justification.fill: The project privatizes every pilot and localized moment in the attainable higher-order construction and proves a raw-estimator remainder bound uniformly over every finite higher-order basis dimension.  The downstream center is clipped before interval formation; projection onto \([-1,1]\) preserves the remainder event for the bounded causal target and guarantees a nonempty reported interval on every transcript.  The resulting interval has uniform finite-sample coverage and phase-sensitive mean interval length at most \(C(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}})\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).  A fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\) also restricts to the attainable class.  Selecting publicly between the two constructions and transferring the ordinary uniform-design lower witness gives, under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\), the attainable bracket with lower endpoint \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\) and upper endpoint \(C\min\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}},1\wedge[n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}]\}\).  The higher-order upper is not transferred to the unchanged full class, whose exact frontier remains unresolved.

prose_updates.related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) establish the privacy-free pointwise CATE rate and motivate the higher-order local-polynomial architecture.  Their upper theorem uses its stated design-density and population-Gram conditions; here the higher-order identities and raw-estimator remainder are certified for the uniform-design attainable construction, including arbitrary finite basis rank, and downstream clipping changes neither calculation nor sensitivity.  KBRW's density-hole fuzzy lower is not asserted to transfer to the present full class with a positive anchor density band.  On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the paper instead combines its nonempty private higher-order interval with the restricted fixed-dimensional direct-regression interval and proves an ordinary two-law lower using uniform-design attainable witnesses.  The resulting bracket is nonsharp but the selector can strictly improve the higher-order upper.  The separate full-class result remains the ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower versus the \(\beta\)-smooth direct-regression upper.  Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008) supply the higher-order influence-function perspective behind the attainable quadratic correction.  Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) motivate honest fixed-length intervals that expose worst-case smoothing bias.  Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) provide nonprivate doubly robust CATE bands in a lower-dimensional heterogeneity problem.  Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025) study private orthogonal CATE learning but do not derive this pointwise Hölder coverage and length phase; Schröder, Hartenstein, and Feuerriegel (2025) treat private intervals for the regular population ATE.  Shoham, Shenfeld, Velner-Harris, and Ligett (2026) give an asymptotic resampling conversion for private estimators, whereas the present intervals use explicit uniform finite-sample bias control.  Dwork and Roth (2014) provide the Gaussian mechanism and post-processing fact used by both private constructions.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-order privacy term comes from the global sensitivity \(m^{-1}(h^{-d}+kh^{-2d})\) of the clipped quadratic-moment release and is proved only as an attainable-submodel upper cost.  Center clipping is downstream and does not reduce this sensitivity or alter the raw-estimator remainder.  The separate full-class direct-regression release has sensitivity \(O((nh^d)^{-1})\) but incurs armwise bias \(O(h^\beta)\), so it does not determine whether the smoother \(\gamma\)-contrast, the nuisance interaction \(q\), or a stabilized private Gram controls the sharp frontier.  The invalid paired-microcell transport step is not revived.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Settled results are replacement privacy and uniform finite-sample coverage of the explicit clipped-center higher-order interval on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), including the unchanged raw-estimator remainder, nonemptiness on every transcript, unrestricted finite basis rank, and achieved length upper \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\).  The attainable-class nonsharp minimax bracket takes the better of that interval and the restricted direct-regression interval; its lower witness has uniform design and satisfies every attainable assumption.  The attainable higher-order upper is not transferred to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}}\).  On the full class, the ordinary lower and fixed-dimensional direct-regression upper give \(c[n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\vee\{1\wedge(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)}\}]\le\mathcal L_n^*(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{full}})\le C[1\wedge\{n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\}]\) under \(L_\pi\ge\kappa\), \(\delta_n\le c_0/n\), and sufficiently large \(n\).  Whether either bracket is tight, including whether a \(q\)-driven or private-Gram branch is unavoidable, remains unresolved.  After the present re-certification, \(\mathrm{oeq{:}sharp\text{-}full\text{-}class\text{-}length\text{-}frontier}\) is the only open statement.

statement_notes.justification: The uniform raw-estimator envelope controls localization bias, higher-order nuisance bias, sampling fluctuation, and Gaussian release noise before any center clipping; downstream projection leaves this proof unchanged.
statement_notes.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 gives an expected-error decomposition without privacy or coverage; ArmstrongKolesar2020 treats worst-case smoothing bias without causal higher-order nuisance bias.
statement_notes.consumer: The bound gives investigators a finite-sample radius that remains valid when low nuisance smoothness makes first-order CATE intervals undercover.

statement_notes.justification: The headline converts the fully privatized higher-order CATE learner into an honest, transcript-wise nonempty pointwise causal interval: projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase error from the bounded target.
statement_notes.gap: SchroederHartensteinFeuerriegel2025 proves a private interval for the regular population ATE, while no located theorem gives uniform pointwise Hölder CATE coverage with higher-order nuisance bias.
statement_notes.consumer: A hospital can release a nonempty confidence interval for the treatment effect at a prespecified anchor point while protecting every record.

statement_notes.justification: The proposition records the strongest certified two-sided mean-length result on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) by combining the transcript-wise nonempty higher-order interval with the restricted full-class direct interval.
statement_notes.gap: Its ordinary \(\gamma\)-smooth lower endpoint does not determine whether either attainable upper branch is minimax sharp, and it does not close the full-class open frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: A study designer can use a public rate comparison to select the narrower of two private honest nonempty pointwise CATE intervals without paying privacy composition.
